summary: Document the content-tool Python requirements and have tools/bootstrap.py report them. tools/content/README.md is the single place for the install command and now names Pillow and openpyxl; the root README points to it. Bootstrap checks exact name==version pins with a strict comparison, lists other lines as not checked, and only warns: an unreadable or undecodable requirements file or a bad pin never changes its exit code, and it never runs pip. The warning names the running interpreter, the absolute requirements path and check.sh's L5R_PYTHON/python3/python order. tools/test_bootstrap.py (9 tests) runs from tools/check.sh. Follows the unhappy-path review and the consistency audit of PR #508.
validation: Windows 11, Git Bash, Python 3.14: bash tools/check.sh --skip-client, All requested checks passed (Python 45+135+6+9 tests OK; 2200/2200 engine, AI, server and transport). 5 of the 9 bootstrap tests fail against the first commit's bootstrap.py. Live python tools/bootstrap.py: Ready, exit 0. Client unchanged; full client check passed on the earlier rebase. Not run on macOS.
remaining: Umbrella #507 stays open: Godot .import churn on first import and csharp-ls needing DOTNET_ROOT are recorded there, not fixed. The consistency audit also noted pre-existing inconsistencies for the leads: check.sh lists top-level tools tests one per line, and test files load modules in two styles.
